finalText:
Redis died, and the app never recovered from it. Here's the timeline.

Redis dropped at 02:14:07 (`connect ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.12:6379`). The app fell back to hitting the database directly, and every service (api, worker-1, worker-2, scheduler) started timing out after 5 seconds under the extra load.

From there it just got worse. The request queue climbed steadily, from 52 to 568, over a max of 500. Redis reconnect attempts fired every couple minutes (7 through 12) and every single one failed — Redis never came back.

At 02:31:44, worker-2 ran out of memory from the backlog and crashed. The supervisor restarted it, but 7 seconds later the whole api process was unresponsive, so the supervisor killed the process group. Service went down at 02:31:52.

So the root cause is the Redis host at `10.0.0.12` going unreachable, and no circuit breaker or backpressure to stop the queue from growing unbounded while it was down. Worth checking why that Redis instance dropped, and adding a cap on queue depth so a cache outage doesn't turn into an OOM crash.
